clue.text: Trouble in sight during fal! 1

definitions.meaning: an eye condition in which the lens clouds over and blurs vision
a large waterfall, especially a steep one on a big river

explanation.surface: Someone's eyesight fails them just as they take a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a clouding of the eye's lens and a great waterfall, so it covers an eye problem and a fall of water.

clue.text: Isolated motorway exit

explanation.surface: A lonely slip road leading off a motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A place that is isolated has been separated from its surroundings, and a highway turn-off is a road branching away from the main route.

clue.text: Account to National Trust for gift

parts.note: a tale is a story or account of events
NT is the usual abbreviation for the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: Someone giving a written report to a heritage charity in return for a present.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity that looks after historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural gift is an innate ability, the flair someone is born with.

clue.text: Do the dirty on female? Certainly

parts.note: to rat on someone is to betray them
her is a pronoun for a female

explanation.surface: Asked whether to betray a woman, someone answers with an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rather!' is a dated British exclamation of enthusiastic agreement, meaning 'yes indeed'.
explanation.definitionFit: As an exclamation of agreement the word means 'yes indeed', an emphatic assent.

clue.text: Stop American state getting inflamed over one part of the week

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece placed over another comes before it

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California
lit means set alight, burning
a is the indefinite article, meaning one
a day is one part of a week

explanation.surface: A call to halt an American state that gets fired up for one weekday.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'over' puts CAL and LIT above A and DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stop working for the time being, to finish for now.

clue.text: Drink is able to travel third-class return

indicators.note: a return trip goes back the way it came, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: can means is able
to go is to travel
C is the third grade after A and B

explanation.surface: Someone who can afford only cheap tickets still manages a trip home for a brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns CAN + GO + C, CANGOC, end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a French brandy, a kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Become too big for gown — tour re-organised

indicators.note: something re-organised has had its parts put in a new arrangement, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A child who has grown too big for a dress, so the trip is planned again.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-organised' rearranges GOWN and TOUR. 'Become' is read as a past participle, as in 'have become too big for'.
explanation.definitionFit: A child who has grown out of clothes has got too large to fit them.

clue.text: Being without water-crowd stockman

parts.note: a neat spirit is served undiluted, with no water added
a herd is a crowd or throng

explanation.surface: A cattleman stuck with a thirsty crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: NEATHERD is an old word for a cowherd: 'neat' once meant cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A neatherd tends cattle, so is a herdsman, an old word for one who looks after livestock.

clue.text: Study stupid contract

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
dense means slow-witted or stupid

explanation.surface: Someone reading over a foolish legal agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract is to shrink or compress, making something smaller or more compact.

clue.text: Sneak is reveal'ng

definitions.meaning: a sneak is a schoolchild who informs on others

explanation.surface: A school informer is giving the game away.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolboy sneak tattles on classmates, and a telltale sign betrays what was meant to stay secret.

clue.text: Pressure on Southern Railway

parts.note: a train is what runs on a railway

explanation.surface: Stress building on a British rail line serving the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Strain is tension or stress, the load placed on something.

clue.text: Receiver has racket enclosed

parts.note: a fence is a criminal receiver of stolen goods
din means a loud noise or racket

explanation.surface: A handler of stolen goods runs a scam shut away somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hemmed in means surrounded or shut in on all sides.

clue.text: Span that is becoming for a boy

parts.note: an arch spans a gap, like a bridge
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A bridge's span that suits a young lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Archie is a boy's name, a pet form of Archibald.

clue.text: Cut northern drill for tidal wave

parts.note: to sever is to cut
to bore is to drill a hole

explanation.surface: Instructions for cutting and drilling in the north, then a great wave arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: The Severn is Britain's longest river; its bore is a wave that runs upstream on high tides.
explanation.definitionFit: A bore is a surge of water travelling upriver on a rising tide, and the Severn has the best known in Britain.

clue.text: Utility of crying

definitions.meaning: a plant supplying water to the public, a public utility
turning on the ... is slang for bursting into tears

explanation.surface: A public water supply that weeps.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a water-supply plant and, informally, a bout of tears.

clue.text: Insist on maintaining demand for project

definitions.meaning: to hold out for a demand
to project is to jut from a surface

explanation.surface: Unions holding firm for their claim over a building scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold out for terms is to persist in demanding them, and something that juts beyond a surface protrudes.

clue.text: Is Ammunition enclosed with patient report

parts.note: a bullet is a round of ammunition
in means inside, enclosed

explanation.surface: Ammunition is sealed inside along with a hospital update.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital issues a bulletin, an official statement, on a patient's condition.

clue.text: Whodunit: excites her till right ending

indicators.note: something that excites stirs things up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right, and ending says it is placed at the close

explanation.surface: A detective novel keeps a reader gripped until the satisfying final pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excites' scrambles HER and TILL to THRILLE, and R for 'right' is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A whodunit is a detective story, one kind of suspense novel.

clue.text: Inflammatory material could affect journal's feelings

parts.note: to touch someone is to affect them emotionally
a paper is a journal or newspaper

explanation.surface: Rabble-rousing copy that could stir a newspaper's emotions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feelings' completes the sense of TOUCH: to affect someone's feelings is to touch them.
explanation.definitionFit: Touch paper is the fuse paper on a firework, lit to set it off, so it is made to catch fire.

clue.text: Baby-sitter taking umbrage !

parts.note: a child carer who looks after the baby, and also one who objects, since to mind is both to look after and to take offence

explanation.surface: A nanny gets in a huff.
explanation.definitionFit: A child carer looks after children, and someone who takes offence objects, both senses of the verb to mind.

clue.text: Green Conservative permit

parts.note: to allow is to permit

explanation.surface: An environmentalist politician grants a Tory a licence.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or immature, like a raw youth.

clue.text: Vigorous man comes over all aesthetic

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece coming over another sits above it

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
arty means having artistic pretensions

explanation.surface: A robust chap suddenly turns arty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes over all' is the idiom for suddenly feeling a certain way; here 'comes over' sets HE above ARTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty means energetic and robust, full of strength and enthusiasm.

clue.text: Cheer-leader worn out by visit

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of cheer is used

parts.note: all in means exhausted

explanation.surface: A cheerleader exhausted by a social call.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop in on someone is to pay them a short visit.

clue.text: I meant it to become confidential

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are to become a different word, shuffled into new order

explanation.surface: Someone insists a remark was meant to be kept private.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimate details are private ones, shared only in confidence.

clue.text: Do better in the air with striking cunning

parts.note: workers out are on strike
fly is slang for sharp or cunning

explanation.surface: A pilot beats rivals in the sky through bold, clever flying.
explanation.definitionFit: To outfly is to surpass others in flight.

clue.text: Lord once stumbled into sympathiser

indicators.note: stumbling is tripping about, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A peer tripped and fell into someone offering sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: A condoler expresses sympathy to the bereaved.

clue.text: Net return on river holding

indicators.note: a return goes back, so the word net is read backwards

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Profit on a river property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns NET to TEN; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenure is the holding of land or office, the right to occupy it.

clue.text: Madcap cry? A peculiarity

parts.note: to tear up is to cry, and a tear is shed in crying
a way is a habit or peculiarity, as in set in one's ways

explanation.surface: A wild person sobs at a strange quirk.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearaway is a reckless, unruly youngster, someone wild and impetuous.
